title: Centrus Signs Contract with Department of Energy for $900 Million Award; Intends to Transition HALEU Production Cascade to Commercial Operation
summary: Centrus Energy (NYSE: LEU) today announced that it has signed a contract to finalize the terms of the competitively-awarded, $900 million task order it received from the U.S. Department of Energy earlier this year. The award will support deployment of large-scale production capacity for High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU) as part of Centrus’ multi-billion-dollar capacity expansion that will include Low-Enriched Uranium (LEU) as well as HALEU.
body_text: Total Enrichment Contract Valued at over $1 Billion, Including All Options Completes Production of Additional 900 Kilograms of HALEU UF6 Ahead of Schedule Prior Contract Extended for Three Months Ahead of Transition Bethesda, MD – Centrus Energy (NYSE: LEU) today announced that it has signed a contract to finalize the terms of the competitively-awarded, $900 million task order it received from the U.S. Department of Energy earlier this year. The award will support deployment of large-scale production capacity for High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU) as part of Centrus’ multi-billion-dollar capacity expansion that will include Low-Enriched Uranium (LEU) as well as HALEU. “Today’s announcement marks another milestone in our expansion, as we pivot from a technology demonstration contract to the new, larger contract aimed at commercial scale production,” said Centrus President and CEO Amir Vexler. “The government’s investment from this contract will be matched several times over with billions of dollars in capital, including other non-dilutive, non-debt funding as well as customer contracts to restore America’s ability to enrich uranium at a large scale.” Transitioning from Demonstration to Commercialization Centrus won a contract in 2019 to build a cascade of advanced centrifuges in Piketon to demonstrate HALEU production with U.S. technology. That demonstration contract was modified and extended in 2022 to allow for a longer period of HALEU production, and was previously extended through June 30, 2026. While Centrus and the Department have signed a three-month, $15 million extension for HALEU storage, Centrus has now completed all HALEU production called for under the existing demonstration contract. Production of the final 900 kilograms of HALEU UF6 required under that contract was completed in mid-June, two weeks ahead of schedule, with a cumulative total of more than 1,900 kilograms produced over the life of the contract. With its large-scale expansion underway, Centrus is transitioning from the old demonstration contract to commercialization with the newer, larger enrichment contract. The first new capacity is expected to come online by 2029. In the interim, Centrus intends to privately operate the existing HALEU cascade on a commercial basis to begin supplying the near-term needs of its customers. Centrus is working with the Department on agreements to enable that transition, including a long-term lease extension for the American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio. The new, fixed-price HALEU Enrichment contract calls for Centrus to deploy commercial-scale HALEU production capacity in Piketon. It also includes options, at the Department’s discretion, for up to $170 million in HALEU purchases for Departmental missions, the total contract value with all options included is $1.07 billion. Modular Enrichment Capacity Build-Out As previously disclosed, Centrus’ modular enrichment capacity build out will based on customer demand and capital resources. The initial build-out will include 12 metric tons of annual HALEU production capacity as well as capacity to meet Centrus existing LEU backlog of $2.4 billion. Subject to customer demand, Centrus can continue expanding production of HALEU and LEU to meet market requirements. Importantly, Centrus’ expects the initial build-out to allow it to achieve nth-of-a-kind centrifuge manufacturing costs. Centrus’ multi-billion-dollar expansion project is expected to support thousands of American jobs, including: 1,000 construction jobs and 300 new operating jobs in Ohio, while retaining 150 existing jobs at the Piketon plant. 430 jobs at Centrus’ centrifuge manufacturing plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, and hundreds of additional jobs across Centrus’ nationwide network of suppliers. Thousands of indirect jobs in Ohio, Tennessee and across the country. The expansion is underpinned by public and private funding along with commercial contracts, a framework that includes: national security missions, third party investments such as prepayment, direct foreign investment, LEU and HALEU commercial contracts, and Centrus’ strong capital position. About Centrus Energy Centrus Energy is a trusted American supplier of nuclear fuel and services for the nuclear power industry, helping meet the growing need for clean, affordable, carbon-free energy. Since 1998, the Company has provided its utility customers with more than 1,850 reactor years of fuel, which is equivalent to more than 7 billion tons of coal. With world-class technical and engineering capabilities, Centrus is pioneering production of High-Assay, Low-Enriched Uranium and is leading the effort to restore America’s uranium enrichment capabilities at scale so that we can meet our clean energy, energy security, and national security needs. Find out more at www.centrusenergy.com or follow us on LinkedIn and X. title: Qnity Powers the Transition from Shrink to Stack with Advanced Packaging Solutions
summary: Qnity launches its Advanced Packaging Innovation Hub, showcasing materials and process technologies for AI infrastructure, HBM, chiplet architectures, hybrid bonding, TSVs, IC substrates and next-generation semiconductor packaging.
body_text: Qnity’s material innovations enable next-generation advanced packaging, showcased through new Innovation Hub WILMINGTON, Del., June 22, 2026 — Qnity Electronics, Inc. (“Qnity”) (NYSE: Q), a premier technology solutions leader across the semiconductor value chain, today announced the launch of its Advanced Packaging Innovation Hub , underscoring advanced packaging as a strategic growth driver and innovation priority for the company. The new online platform showcases Qnity’s breadth of material and technology solutions designed for advanced packaging, enabling the next generation of artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing, cloud, networking, and edge computing systems. A Strategic Growth Engine for the Future The semiconductor industry is moving beyond the traditional gains of Moore's Law, and innovation is increasingly shifting from "shrink" to "stack" through the design of advanced 3D architectures. Advanced packaging is one of the most important enabling technologies for AI infrastructure and next-generation computing, making it a key focus area for Qnity's long-term growth and innovation strategy. “As AI reshapes computing, the hardest engineering problems are moving into the connections between chips, layer to layer — where performance, power, density, and reliability are decided," said Chuck Xu, President, Interconnect Solutions at Qnity. "That's where Qnity shines. We bring our semiconductor and interconnect strengths together so customers can master advanced packaging from design through system integration, end-to-end.” Solutions for the Advanced Packaging Era As system architectures evolve beyond conventional packaging approaches, advanced packaging has emerged as a critical driver of performance, power, and efficiency. Across the advanced packaging stack—from High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and interposers to bonding, assembly, and IC substrates—Qnity provides materials and process technologies that help customers achieve the yield, process control, reliability, and performance required for increasingly complex heterogeneous system designs. Advanced chip manufacturers face growing demands for high-density interconnects, through-silicon vias (TSVs), fine-line redistribution layers (RDLs), advanced metallization, hybrid bonding, and multi-die integration. Qnity's solutions enable precise manufacturing, defect reduction, thermal management, high-density routing, and long-term device reliability. Together, these capabilities help customers overcome manufacturing challenges in advanced packaging. Learn More Explore Qnity's Advanced Packaging Innovation Hub to learn how the company's solutions are enabling the future of AI-driven computing. About Qnity Qnity is a premier technology solutions provider across the semiconductor value chain, empowering AI, high performance computing, and advanced connectivity. From groundbreaking solutions for semiconductor chip manufacturing, to enabling high-speed transmission within complex electronic systems, our high-performance materials and integration expertise make tomorrow’s technologies possible. More information about the company, its businesses and solutions can be found at www.qnityelectronics.com . Qnity™, the Qnity Node Logo, and all products, unless otherwise noted, denoted with ™ or ® are trademarks, trade names or registered trademarks of affiliates of Qnity Electronics, Inc. # # # Media Contact Ashley Boucher ashley.boucher@qnityelectronics.com

title: Teague Announces Plan to Retire January 2027
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Enterprise Products Partners L.P.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Fowler to Succeed Teague as CEO HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 1, 2026-- Enterprise Products Partners L.P. (NYSE: EPD) today reported that A.J. “Jim” Teague, co-chief executive officer of Enterprise’s general partner, has announced his intention to retire as of January 4, 2027. W. Randall “Randy” Fowler, Enterprise’s co-chief executive officer, will serve as chief executive officer effective upon Mr. Teague’s retirement. “Jim has been integral to our success since he joined Enterprise in 1999,” said Randa Duncan, non-executive chairman of Enterprise’s general partner. “Under Jim’s leadership, Enterprise has played a leading role in developing and serving both domestic and international markets for prolific supplies of NGL production from the U.S. shale plays. Enterprise became the first midstream company to provide wellhead to water NGL services in 2009. These efforts have facilitated production and generated incremental revenue for U.S. shale producers, contributed to the renaissance of the U.S. petrochemical industry and provided reliable and affordable U.S. ethane and propane supplies to international markets, which has literally improved the lives of millions of people globally by lifting them out of energy poverty.” “Jim also led Enterprise’s innovation to deliver additional value and flexibility for our petrochemical customers by transitioning a historically opaque contract market for ethylene and polymer-grade propylene on the U.S. Gulf Coast to transparent and liquid pricing and storage hubs for these products in Mont Belvieu, Texas. The industry adoption and success of these pricing points ultimately led to the development of financial futures markets for these products,” continued Ms. Duncan. “Over this period, we have grown the enterprise value of the partnership from $1.8 billion to almost $120 billion. All of us at Enterprise are grateful for Jim’s twenty-eight years of leadership and contributions. We wish him the very best in his future endeavors and a well-deserved retirement. Over the next six months, in addition to his normal duties, Jim will be actively involved in transition activities as we prepare for his retirement,” said Ms. Duncan. “I look forward to continue working with Randy as our chief executive officer to continue to execute on Enterprise’s growth capital investments and pursue new opportunities,” said Ms. Duncan. “Throughout my career, I have been fortunate to experience two exceptionally rewarding chapters,” said Teague. “I spent 22 years with Dow Chemical, where I had the opportunity to travel extensively around the world, serving as Vice President of Hydrocarbon Feedstocks. That experience provided me with a deep appreciation for the global energy and petrochemical landscape, as well as exposure to diverse cultures.” “My 28 years with Enterprise Products have been even more meaningful. I have had the privilege of being part of an organization that has grown far beyond what I could have ever imagined. It has been truly rewarding to witness not only our significant growth in earnings, but also the increasing sophistication of our business as we have learned to fully capture the opportunities within our asset footprint,” stated Teague. “Most importantly, at Enterprise Products I have had the honor of working alongside some of the most talented, dedicated, and principled individuals in our industry. This has been a remarkable journey, and I am deeply proud of the relationships we have built, the experiences we have shared, and the accomplishments we have achieved," said Teague. Mr. Fowler has served as a director of Enterprise’s general partner since 2011 and as Enterprise’s co-chief executive officer since 2020. He also served as our chief financial officer from 2007 to 2015 and then again from 2018 to 2024. He joined Enterprise in 1999, shortly after Enterprise’s initial public offering. Mr. Fowler has 48 years of finance and accounting experience in various sectors of the energy industry. Upon Mr. Teague’s retirement, Enterprise’s general partner will expand the Office of the Chairman, which is a management oversight group that serves as a liaison between the board of Enterprise’s general partner and senior management. Currently, the Office of the Chairman is comprised of Ms. Duncan serving as non-executive chairman, Richard H. “Hank” Bachmann serving as vice chairman of Enterprise’s general partner, and Teague and Fowler each serving as co-chief executive officers. Upon Mr. Teague’s retirement, the Office of the Chairman will be comprised of Ms. Duncan, Mr. Bachmann, Mr. Fowler, Michael C. “Tug” Hanley serving as chief commercial officer and R. Daniel Boss serving as chief financial officer. Enterprise Products Partners L.P. is one of the largest publicly traded partnerships and a leading North American provider of midstream energy services to producers and consumers of natural gas, NGLs, crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals. Our services include: natural gas gathering, treating, processing, transportation and storage; NGL transportation, fractionation, storage and import and export terminals; crude oil and refined products transportation, storage and terminals; petrochemical transportation and services; and a marine transportation business that operates on key U.S. inland and intracoastal waterway systems. The partnership’s assets currently include over 50,000 miles of pipelines; over 300 million barrels of storage capacity for NGLs, crude oil, refined products and petrochemicals; and 14 billion cubic feet of natural gas storage capacity. title: Best Pharma Brand Protection Software in July 2026
summary: See the top brand protection tools for pharma in July 2026, covering counterfeit drugs, fake pharmacy sites, grey market tracking, and AI-driven
body_text: Your grey market enforcement needs are not the same as your counterfeit drug detection needs, and your fake pharmacy problem is a third thing entirely. That distinction matters more than most pharmaceutical brand protection software vendors would like you to think. If you're building or rebuilding a pharma brand protection stack in 2026 and want to know which tools cover which threats without taking vendor claims at face value, this is where to start. ‍ TLDR: ‍ The WHO reports one in ten medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified, making detection speed a patient safety issue, and a revenue one too. Counterfeit drug listings can copy packaging while stripping all trademark use, so tools without SKU-level image detection miss a large share of infringing inventory. Fake pharmacy sites evade standard monitoring by hiding behind privacy-protected WHOIS records and geo-cloaking, requiring registrar-level relationships to take them down. Grey market enforcement and counterfeit enforcement need different evidence: IP claims for fakes, inventory leakage tracing and distributor matching for unauthorized channel sales. MarqVision covers marketplace detection, grey market channel enforcement, fake pharmacy takedown, and physical test purchase verification inside one system. ‍ ‍ ‍ What Are Pharmaceutical Brand Protection Tools? Pharmaceutical brand protection tools are the software and services that help drug makers find and take down threats to their products across the internet. In practice, that means detecting counterfeit drugs online, enforcing authorized distribution channels, shutting down fake pharmacy websites, and tracking grey market sales of prescription products moving outside sanctioned supply chains. ‍ What sets this category apart from fashion or electronics enforcement is the stakes. A fake handbag disappoints a buyer. A falsified medicine can contain the wrong dose, the wrong active ingredient, or none at all, and the World Health Organization reports that one in ten medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified. ‍ That patient safety dimension raises the bar. Detection speed and enforcement completeness carry weight here that pure revenue-loss calculations never fully capture. ‍ ‍ How We Ranked These Tools We did not run hands-on trials of every tool below. This ranking draws on vendor documentation, published case studies, marketplace coverage disclosures, and buyer reviews on sites like G2. Weigh each criterion against your own threat profile before shortlisting. ‍ Here is what a pharma legal, IP, or brand protection team should assess: ‍ Breadth of marketplace and social media coverage, including regional pharmacies and messaging apps where illicit sales cluster, a core criterion when assessing online brand protection tools Detection accuracy for counterfeit drug listings, especially those copying packaging while stripping trademark use Enforcement speed and documented takedown success rates across platforms Grey market monitoring and unauthorized seller enforcement, including seller matching and distribution leakage tracing Fake pharmacy and phishing site takedown, from domain detection through registrar-level removal AI-driven detection automation that cuts analyst review time Support for physical product verification through test purchases, since formulation-level fakes cannot be confirmed from listing images alone ‍ ‍ ‍ Best Overall Pharma Brand Protection Tool: MarqVision We built MarqVision for the threat mix pharma teams manage daily: counterfeit listings, leaked prescription inventory, and fake pharmacy sites appearing faster than manual review can catch. Where single-category tools cover one slice, we run marketplace detection, grey market enforcement, domain takedown, and physical verification inside one system. Core Strengths AI-native Full-Stack Detection compares each listing against genuine product data at the SKU level, reaching 97%+ accuracy and catching counterfeits that copy drug packaging while stripping out any trademark use. Social Media Network Search maps unauthorized seller networks across friend lists, group memberships, and social commerce channels, a capability particularly effective for pharmaceutical enforcement. Digital Risk Protection tracks 1.3B+ domains and removes fake pharmacy sites at a median response time of 5.3 hours (internal data, Q1 2026); see how brand takedown times compare across vendors, working through direct registrar relationships and Google Safe Browsing integration. The grey market module enforces prescription-only distribution restrictions, traces inventory leakage against a database of 600,000 reseller profiles, and issues soft notices to unauthorized distributors through Seller Dialogue. MarqLaw test purchase programs produce ingredient-level physical evidence for cases where a listing looks legitimate but formulation-level counterfeiting can only be confirmed in hand. Rotation-based marketplace monitoring lets you shift coverage as counterfeit drug activity migrates from one channel to the next. ‍ Bottom line: you get AI-driven marketplace detection, grey market channel enforcement, fake pharmacy takedown, and physical test purchase verification in one unified system. ‍ ‍ ‍ Corsearch Corsearch grew through acquisition, folding Incopro, Entura, and Marketly into one trademark and enforcement offering now under private equity ownership. What They Offer Trademark clearance, monitoring, and enforcement across marketplaces and social channels Brand monitoring spanning domains, social media, and unauthorized seller activity Customized enforcement workflows with case management dashboards An AI-enhanced detection system deployed in 2024 ‍ Good for: enterprise pharma brands already running trademark services through Corsearch who want monitoring consolidated inside one vendor. ‍ Limitation: accounts report the 2024 AI deployment has not shown measurable detection gains, and analyst-hours pricing layered on brand protection software fees can push annual spend toward $60,000, straining mid-market budgets. ‍ Bottom line: Corsearch fits large IP portfolios focused on trademark consolidation, but teams wanting transparent AI-driven enforcement metrics and cost-efficient grey market coverage will find a more accountable option elsewhere. ‍ ‍ ‍ OpSec Security OpSec Security, now part of Crane NXT, pairs physical product authentication with digital brand monitoring, and it has served pharmaceutical and luxury brands for decades. Its heritage sits in on-product security features, not automated online enforcement. What They Offer Physical product authentication through holograms, forensic markers, optical elements, and serialized labels Online marketplace and domain monitoring for counterfeit and infringing listings Track-and-trace supply chain compliance and serialization for compliance-driven industries, including pharma ‍ Good for: pharma companies needing physical authentication tied to digital enforcement, particularly those already managing serialization under the Drug Supply Chain Security Act. ‍ Limitation: OpSec's digital enforcement runs on analyst-hours billing and a sequential cease-and-desist cycle, producing slower response times than vendors using direct registrar relationships and automated workflows, a gap noted in third-party marketplace reviews . ‍ Bottom line: teams whose primary threat is online counterfeit drug listings and fake pharmacy sites will want faster AI-driven enforcement than this legacy workflow delivers. ‍ ‍ ‍ MarkMonitor MarkMonitor, acquired by Com Laude in January 2026, launched an updated intelligence-led brand protection suite in April 2026, building on its history in domain portfolio management, anti-cybersquatting, and trademark enforcement for enterprise brands. What They Offer Corporate domain portfolio management, DNS security, and domain acquisition Automated and manual takedowns for infringing websites and social media content UDRP filings and ccTLD dispute resolution Cease-and-desist programs and anonymous domain acquisition for strategic asset recovery ‍ Good for: pharma brands whose primary threat is domain abuse, cybersquatting, and branded drug name impersonation sites, and that want deep registrar expertise paired with enforcement. ‍ Limitation: MarkMonitor's roots sit in a lawyer-driven, per-action model, and every enforcement recommendation in the 2026 suite is still manually reviewed by experts, making it slower to scale against high-volume counterfeit listings or widespread grey market enforcement. ‍ Bottom line: MarkMonitor suits enterprise teams with complex domain portfolios and drug-name cybersquatting exposure, but brands needing automated marketplace and grey market enforcement at scale will find an AI-native full-stack approach more efficient. ‍ ‍ ‍ Red Points Red Points focuses on automated counterfeit detection and marketplace enforcement, with most of its client base in the small and mid-market segment. It runs a delegated enforcement model, so your team confirms each infringement detection before any takedown fires. What They Offer Automated counterfeit product detection across global e-commerce marketplaces Image similarity scoring with customer-set thresholds that trigger takedowns Social media and domain monitoring for brand abuse Revenue recovery backed by litigation support Good for: smaller pharma or consumer health brands wanting a self-service detection tool with low entry cost. ‍ Limitation: Red Points caps copyrighted product images at 50 per plan, skips enforcement on major Chinese social commerce channels including Pinduoduo, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu, and teams dealing with unauthorized sellers on Amazon will find its managed enforcement add-on costly, and prices managed enforcement as an enterprise add-on at $5,000 per month above the base fee. For pharma brands with China exposure and lean teams, those gaps compound fast. ‍ Bottom line: Red Points fits small and mid-market consumer health brands that self-manage enforcement reviews, but companies with global distribution or Chinese market exposure outgrow its structural limits quickly. ‍ ‍ ‍ BrandShield BrandShield concentrates on fake website detection, phishing takedown, and the cybersecurity threats tied to online fraud, extending monitoring across social media, domains, and domain impersonation . What They Offer Fake website and phishing site detection and takedown Social media brand impersonation monitoring across major platforms Counterfeit seller detection on e-commerce channels Domain monitoring for brand abuse and cybersquatting ‍ Good for: pharma brands whose main worry is fake online pharmacy sites, phishing portals cloning branded patient or prescriber drug portals, and direct-to-consumer fraud. ‍ Limitation: BrandShield publishes no Mean Time to Resolution figures, leaving pharma legal teams without a measurable SLA. Its cybersecurity emphasis also leaves grey market channel enforcement and unauthorized seller network monitoring thinly covered. ‍ Bottom line: BrandShield handles phishing and fake pharmacy site threats well for cybersecurity-led use cases, but teams needing marketplace counterfeit enforcement, grey market tracing, and social seller detection in one place will find broader coverage elsewhere. ‍ ‍ ‍ Feature Comparison Table of Pharma Brand Protection Tools Compare the six tools across the capabilities pharma teams weigh most before shortlisting. ‍ Capability MarqVision Corsearch OpSec MarkMonitor Red Points BrandShield AI-native detection Yes Partial No Manual only Yes Yes Marketplace counterfeit enforcement Yes Yes Yes Limited Yes Limited Grey market and unauthorized seller monitoring Yes Yes Limited No Add-on No Fake pharmacy and phishing site takedown Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Chinese marketplace and social coverage Yes Limited Limited Limited No Limited Physical test purchase programs Yes No No No No No Prescription distribution enforcement Yes No No No No No Fully managed enforcement included Yes Yes Yes Manual Add-on Yes ‍ ‍ ‍ FAQ What is the difference between counterfeit drug enforcement and grey market enforcement online? Counterfeit enforcement targets falsified products: fake pills and supplements , cloned packaging, listings passing off unauthorized goods as genuine. Grey market enforcement targets authentic drugs sold outside sanctioned channels by unauthorized resellers who bypass prescription controls or distribution agreements. The evidence differs too. Counterfeit cases lean on IP claims and product verification; grey market cases hinge on tracing inventory leakage and matching sellers against authorized distributor lists. Do these tools work for both branded and generic pharma companies? Yes, though threat weighting varies. Branded manufacturers face heavier drug-name cybersquatting and packaging counterfeiting. Generic makers see more grey market diversion and unauthorized reseller activity, a pattern driving adoption of AI brand protection platforms over legacy models. If your primary exposure is brand-name impersonation, lead with domain and fake-pharmacy takedown. If it is channel leakage, weight seller matching and prescription distribution enforcement first. How do test purchase programs support online pharmaceutical enforcement? When a listing looks legitimate from images and text alone, a test buy is the only way to confirm formulation-level counterfeiting. Physical inspection surfaces mismatched lot numbers, missing seals, and off-spec contents that platforms increasingly demand before acting on a report. For pharma, the test buy doubles as both authentication and the evidentiary record a takedown request needs. Why is fake online pharmacy detection harder than counterfeit listings? Rogue pharmacies spin up new domains constantly, hide behind privacy-protected WHOIS records, and geo-cloak content to evade monitoring. They also live outside marketplace reporting frameworks, so takedown depends on registrar relationships and hosting-provider unmasking instead of standard complaint forms. Why does jurisdiction-specific trademark registration matter for enforcement? Platforms and courts act on registered marks. A mark registered in the EU may not satisfy enforcement requirements on a US marketplace storefront, and paid ad takedowns stall without a registration in the jurisdiction where the ad appears. Audit your registrations against every market where you enforce before scoping a program. Why MarqVision Is the Best Pharma Brand Protection Tool For pharma teams, the deciding factor is whether one vendor can close the gaps others leave open. We do that by pairing Social Media Network Search, built expressly for pharmaceutical seller networks, with Full-Stack Detection that flags counterfeit drug listings even when they strip out every trademark. Add prescription distribution enforcement in the grey market module, and you can act on channel leakage that IP claims alone cannot reach. The result is fewer handoffs and less exposure sitting unresolved. When a listing looks clean but the formulation is suspect, MarqLaw test purchases put physical evidence in hand, so your takedown request carries the proof platforms now demand. ‍ ‍ FAQ How do I choose between MarqVision, Corsearch, OpSec, MarkMonitor, Red Points, and BrandShield for pharma brand protection? Start with your primary threat vector. If counterfeit drug listings and grey market channel leakage dominate your exposure, weight tools with AI-native marketplace detection and seller matching: MarqVision and Corsearch cover both, though Corsearch skews toward large trademark portfolios. If domain abuse and drug-name cybersquatting are the core problem, MarkMonitor's registrar depth is purpose-built for that. If your budget is lean and your enforcement team is self-managed, Red Points fits, though its gaps surface quickly once China exposure or prescription distribution enforcement enters the picture. BrandShield handles phishing and fake pharmacy sites well but leaves grey market and marketplace enforcement thinly covered. When is physical test purchasing necessary instead of relying on digital detection alone? Any time a listing replicates branded packaging but formulation-level counterfeiting is the actual threat. Image recognition and text analysis cannot detect substituted active ingredients, off-spec dosages, or missing seals; that confirmation only comes from handling the product. For pharma, the test buy also doubles as evidentiary documentation: platforms increasingly reject takedown requests supported only by website images, requiring physical inspection photos showing lot numbers, packaging details, and authentication features before they will act. Is MarqVision better than Red Points for pharma companies with Chinese marketplace exposure? For pharma teams with material China exposure, MarqVision covers the channel; Red Points structurally does not. Red Points caps copyrighted product images at 50 per plan and skips enforcement on Pinduoduo, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu, the channels where counterfeit drugs and unauthorized prescription products cluster heavily. If your enforcement program requires action on Chinese social commerce channels or prescription distribution monitoring, Red Points' structural limits create gaps that compound quickly for pharma-specific use cases. What should pharma legal teams check before scoping a grey market enforcement program? Audit your trademark registrations against every jurisdiction where you plan to enforce before signing any contract. Platforms act on registered marks, and a mark registered in the EU may not satisfy enforcement requirements on a US marketplace storefront. For prescription distribution enforcement in particular, confirm whether the vendor's seller matching capability can cross-reference your authorized distributor list against a reseller database; this is the mechanism that traces inventory leakage, and not every tool on this list offers it. Why does fake online pharmacy detection require different capabilities than marketplace counterfeit enforcement? Rogue pharmacies operate outside marketplace reporting frameworks entirely, so standard complaint forms do not apply. Takedown depends on registrar relationships, hosting-provider unmasking, and Google Safe Browsing integration, not IP claims filed through a marketplace portal. They also spin up new domains continuously and geo-cloak content to evade monitoring built on periodic scraping cycles. The enforcement path runs through abuse reporting channels, WHOIS unmasking, and direct registrar engagement, a separate capability stack from the marketplace detection and takedown workflows that handle counterfeit drug listings. Final Thoughts on Fighting Counterfeit Drugs and Grey Market Enforcement Patient safety makes pharmaceutical brand protection different from every other enforcement category, and that raises the bar on detection speed, enforcement completeness, and the depth of coverage you need across channels. title: Bell celebrates the first IFR-configured Bell 407GXi order in the United Kingdom
summary: “Our team is honored to celebrate this signing," said Robin Wendling, managing director, Europe, Bell.
body_text: Bell Textron Inc. announced during Farnborough International Airshow 2026 that it received a signed purchase agreement for an instrument flight rules (IFR)-configured Bell 407GXi , marking the first time that the platform with an IFR configuration kit will be operated by a customer in the United Kingdom. “Our team is honored to celebrate this signing and expand our Bell 407GXi offerings to customers in the United Kingdom,” said Robin Wendling, managing director, Europe, Bell. “The Bell 407GXi has earned its name as a multi-mission workhorse, and we continue to see steady interest in the Bell 407GXi platform across the region.” In addition to the aircraft order, Bell recently completed a demonstration tour with the platform in the United Kingdom, making stops at Lydd Airport, Goodwood, and High Wycombe. “Combining its IFR capability with the platform’s latest Designer Series interior offering, the Bell 407GXi provides customers with the ultimate VIP experience to suit their business needs,” added Wendling. Making its debut in 2025, Bell introduced its new luxury interior options for the Bell 407GXi as part of its Designer Series – a series of offerings that set new standards for Bell interiors. The Bell 407GXi allows operators to seamlessly perform in demanding environments while relying on its Garmin G1000H NXi Flight Deck, an all-glass avionic suite, as it relays critical safety information. To find out more about how Bell aircraft advances missions worldwide, please visit the Bell product page or visit the Bell pavilion (#A031) this week during Farnborough International Airshow 2026 . title: American Society for Reproductive Medicine: Trends from the 2025 Scientific Congress
body_text: The work we do at Carrot matters now more than ever. The Carrot provider partnerships team recently attended the American Society for Reproductive Medicine Scientific Congress & Expo in Denver where over 5,500 professionals gathered around this year’s theme, "Global Collaboration to Advance Reproductive Health." With enthusiastic discussions about metabolic health and male infertility, trends across sthe Congress reinforced the value of Carrot’s approach to providing comprehensive, personalized fertility, hormone, and family-building benefits. Metabolic health, front and center The scientific sessions consistently validated that fertility care requires a comprehensive approach that addresses root causes. This aligns with the concept of the " Premester " — those 3-12 months before pregnancy. Health decisions made during these months, particularly around metabolic health, can dramatically affect fertility outcomes. Research presented at the conference highlighted how conditions rooted in metabolic dysfunction are one of the largest and fastest-growing causes of fertility challenges. Only 12 percent of Americans have ideal metabolic health, and disorders like obesity and blood sugar dysregulation make it harder to get pregnant and lead to lower IVF success rates. This reinforces the power of Sprints , our metabolic-fertility program that focuses on nutrition, movement, sleep, and stress management. Male infertility must be addressed The sessions on male infertility revealed concerning trends about paternal age and its impact on outcomes. Paternal age of 40 and older is associated with declines in semen quality and increased risks for adverse outcomes. In donor cycles, paternal age under 50 correlates with lower miscarriage rates and higher blastocyst yields, demonstrating that male age impacts embryologic metrics in meaningful ways. The Congress also highlighted an unfortunate truth: the stigma about male infertility is real and prevalent. The data on this is limited, especially for marginalized communities, but the fertility journey often isolates men, even though they constitute 50 percent of infertility cases. It’s essential to focus on better education and integrated male health screening as part of comprehensive fertility care. Doors are opening for diverse workforces Meeting with colleagues from across Latin America, Europe, and beyond highlighted both significant progress and persistent gaps in fertility care access. The global nature of ASRM — with clinicians, researchers, and exhibitors from countries around the world — underscored that infertility is truly a global issue. This is particularly relevant as we think about modern workforces and modern benefits. Traditional benefits models are failing to meet the needs of today's distributed, diverse workforce. One-in-six employees struggle with getting pregnant, and 20 percent of the workforce is in some kind of menopause transition, yet most employers offer no support for this major life stage. Moving forward together What resonated most throughout ASRM 2025 was the shared commitment across thousands of attendees to advancing reproductive health for all populations — from preconception through menopause, and across all paths to parenthood. At Carrot, we're proud to be part of this global collaboration, working alongside clinicians, researchers, and advocates who share our vision of making comprehensive fertility and family care accessible worldwide. The insights from ASRM 2025 reinforce our commitment to an evidence-driven approach that prioritizes clinical excellence, addresses root causes, and supports all members through their unique journeys.
